en.value: elongation of the eyeball Choose the correct code-

english.explanation: Myopia (Near sightedness) is caused due to the variation in the distance between the eye lens and retina. This distance increase when the eyeball gets elongated along its axis. Myopia can occur if the eye ball is elongated leading to image formation in front of the retina. It can also occur if refracting power of the lens is affected due to cornea or lens being too curved. This effect can be move pronounced with age. It can be corrected by the concave lens.

en.value: Where are the reflex arcs formed in our body?

english.explanation: A reflex arc is neural pathway that control a reflex. In vertebrates, most sensory neurons do not pass directly into the brain, but synapse in the spinal cord. Sensory neurons carry signals from the receptor organs to the spinal cord where the arc is formed.

en.value: Which of the following phenomenon converts nitrogen into oxides of nitrogen?

english.explanation: Lightning is a natural phenomenon which occurs in the sky and responsible for nitrogen fixation. Lightning is a powerful electrical discharge that occurs during thunderstorms. When lightning strikes the earth, it ionizes the air and generates a lot of heat, which can cause the nitrogen gas (N2) in the atmosphere to react with oxygen gas (O2) and form oxides of nitrogen (NO and NO2).

en.value: What is the average diameter of the eyeball of a human?

english.explanation: The average diameter of the eyeball in a human is around 23 millimeters or 2.3 cm. This measurement refers to the distance across the widest part of the eyeball, from one end to the other. Individual measurement can vary depending on factors such as age, sex, ethnicity, and other factors, but 2.3 cm is a generally accepted average diameter.

en.value: Gustatory receptor is present in -

english.explanation: Taste Receptor of the tongue are present in the taste buds of papillae. There are three types of papillae involved in taste : fungiform papillae, foliate papillae and circumvallate papillae. Gustatory receptors are primarily present on the tongue, along with a few other locations in mouth, including the roof of mouth, the back of the throat, and the epiglottis. These receptors are responsible for the sense of taste and help to perceive the five primary taste sensations : sweet , sour, salty, bitter and Umami (savory).

en.value: The carbohydrates which are not used immediately in plants are stored in which of the following forms?

english.explanation: The plants store their carbohydrates in terms of their usage in the life cycle of the organism. The carbohydrates which are not used immediately are stored in the form of starch in the plants. Fat are stored in the adipose tissues of the living organisms which are located beneath the upper layer of the skin.

en.value: Which of the following is present in the Prokaryotic cell?

english.explanation: Prokaryotic cells lack nuclear envelope, membrane - bound cell organelles like endoplasmic reticulum (ER), lysosomes, mitochondria etc. Cytoplasm is present in a prokaryotic cell. Cytoplasm is a gel-like substance that fills the cell and contains various structures such as ribosomes, DNA and enzymes that are necessary for cellular metabolism.

en.value: Who is known as the father of genetics?

english.explanation: Gregor Johann Mendel - Through his work on pea plant he discovered the fundamental law of inheritance. He is known as father of genetics. Aristotle is called the father of biology. Aristotle distinguished about 500 species of birds, mammal and fishes in History of animals. The invention of the microscope led to the discovery of the cell by Robert Hooke. Isaac Newton was also responsible for working out many of the principles of visible light and the laws of motion and contributing to calculus.

en.value: Which of the following is found in plant cells only?

english.explanation: The plastid is a double - membrane organelle found in the cells of plants and algae. Plastids are semiautonomous organelles that have their own genetic material (i.e. DNA). Plastids are the sites where important chemical compounds used by the cell are manufactured and stored. They are of two main types Leucoplast and Chromoplast. Cell walls, plastids, and a large, central vacuole are absent in animal cells.

en.value: Which of the following is known as malaria parasite?

english.explanation: Malaria is caused by the plasmodium parasite. The parasite can be spread to human through the bites of infected mosquitoes.

en.value: Which of the following parts of living organisms preferentially absorb UV rays, and its high energy breaks the chemical bonds within these molecules?

english.explanation: DNA and Proteins of living organisms preferentially absorb UV rays and its high energy breaks the chemical bond of hydrogen within these molecules. UV rays damages DNA and mutation may occur. It causes ageing of the skin, damage to skin cells and various type of skin cancers.

en.value: It is colourless and odourless gas. Which of the following gases is being talked about

english.explanation: Carbon monoxide (CO) - a colourless, odourless, tasteless and toxic air pollutant produced by the incomplete combustion of carbon - containing fuels such as gasoline, natural gas, oil, Coal and wood.

en.value: Mendel selected how many pairs of contrasting characters of pea plant for his experiment?

english.explanation: Mendel selected seven pairs of contrasting character of pea plant for his experiment which were as follows–pea shape. (round or wrinkled), pea color (green or yellow), pod shape (constricted or inflated), Pod colour - (green or yellow), Flower colour-(Purple or white), Plant size- (Tall or Dwarf) and Position of flowers (axial or terminal).

en.value: Many invertebrates like Planaria and some vertebrates like lizards replace lost body - parts by ____.

english.explanation: Regeneration - Is a process of generating the whole organism from its body part. It is known as process of renewal restoration and growth. Regeneration is fundamentally regulated by asexual cellular process. It is the reactivation of development in post embryonic life to restore missing or damaged tissue.

en.value: Leishmania is a parasitic Protozoa which causes ____disease.

The disease Kala - Azar is caused by the Protozoan Leishmania donovani. Leishmania donovani is a Parasitic protozoan belonging to the class mastigophora or flagellata. Symptoms include cutaneous Leishmaniasis- skin ulcers, weakness, weight loss, and other infections.

en.value: Biomagnification of which of the following can lead to disturbed calcium metabolism and ultimately thinning of eggshells of birds?

english.explanation: Biomagnification refers to an increase in the concentration of the toxicant at successive trophic levels. This happens because a toxic substance accumulated by an organism but cannot be metabolized or excreted by the body and therefore is thus passed on the next higher trophic level which feeds on them. This phenomenon is well known for mercury and DDT. High concentration of DDT through biomagnification disturb calcium metabolism in birds which causes thinning of eggshell and their premature breaking, eventually causing decline in bird populations.

In India Ration cards are primarily used when purchasing subsidized food stuffs and fuel. The introduction of Rationing in India dates back to the 1940s against the backdrop of the Bengal famine.
